consensus_issues.description: ideal-product fails to compute additive closure. The mathematical definition of ideal product I*J requires all finite sums of products {i*j}, not just the individual products.
consensus_issues.suggested_fix: Implement iterative additive closure until no new elements are generated

consensus_issues.description: Functions use built-in 'member' which uses 'equal?' instead of the ring's custom 'ring-equal-fn'. This breaks correctness for rings with complex element structures.
consensus_issues.code_snippet:
(member (ring-add r (car as) (car bs)) i-elems)
(member prod i-elems)
(member a i-elems)
consensus_issues.suggested_fix: Replace all 'member' calls with 'member-equal' using (ring-equal-fn r)

consensus_issues.description: is-maximal-ideal? is a stub that always returns #t for proper ideals. It does not verify the actual maximality condition (no proper ideal contains it).
consensus_issues.code_snippet:
(and (not (member (ring-one r) i-elems))
     ; Check no proper ideal contains it
     #t)))  ; Simplified check
consensus_issues.suggested_fix: Implement maximality check: verify that adding any element not in ideal generates the entire ring

consensus_issues.description: is-prime-ideal? does not verify that the ideal is proper (I != R). Mathematically, the entire ring R cannot be a prime ideal.
make-ring-z creates a structure that violates ring closure axioms. The finite set [-100, 100] is not closed under + or * (e.g., 60+60=120 is outside the set).
consensus_issues.suggested_fix: Either use modular arithmetic or document as approximate/truncated representation

consensus_issues.suggested_fix: Add checks: (member-equal (ring-zero r) i-elems ...) and for all i, (member-equal (ring-neg r i) i-elems ...)

non_consensus_issues.description: is-unit? only checks right-inverse, incorrect for non-commutative rings
make-principal-ideal only produces left ideals, not two-sided ideals for non-commutative rings
